newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian government loses vote on budget amendment.
newsitem.headline: Italian government loses vote on budget amendment.

text.p: The Italian government suffered a small setback in the lower house of parliament on Wednesday when the centre-right opposition passed an amendment to the 1997 budget bill.
The Freedom Alliance's amendment to lower the number of pupils in public schoolrooms passed with 263 votes to 260 with three abstentions during a budget debate in the Chamber of Deputies.
The amendment was expected to involve a slight increase in spending on education, parliamentary sources said.
The budget aims to cut a total of 62.5 trillion lire ($42 billion) from next year's deficit and to enable the country to qualify for European monetary union.

The Chamber, where Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left coalition depends on the support of the hard-left Communist Refoundation for a majority, is expected to finish debating the budget late next week.
It then passes to the Senate, which the government controls. The budget must be passed by law by the end of the year. -- Rome newsroom 396 678 2505
